lines.text: The PearX interview is on November 4 at 2 pm over video.
They told me the PearX interview will cover traction, the team and why now.
The PearX interview is the partner round with two partners.
My PearX interview is for Tidepool, my startup.
My PearX interview answer on traction should lead with the 1,200 weekly users.
I want my PearX interview answer on why now to mention the records move.
I practice my PearX answers with Iris on Sunday nights.
The why now story is that clinics moved their records online in the last two years.
I applied to PearX for the winter batch in September.
Tidepool has 1,200 weekly users across four clinics.
Tidepool books patients for small clinics without phone calls.
The Tidepool team is me and my cofounder Iris Sato, who writes the code.
Tidepool is in a paid pilot and raised a 150,000 dollar pre seed.
The one line pitch is online booking for small clinics that still run on the phone.
Hearth Ventures led the Tidepool pre seed, with two angels.
Tidepool grows about 15 percent a month.
The October investor update leads with the 15 percent growth.
Orrinwood Family Clinic was the first Tidepool pilot.
Bayview Pediatrics books about 300 visits a week on Tidepool.
Elm Street Dental joined the Tidepool pilot in July.
Lakeside Physical Therapy wants text reminders from Tidepool.
Tidepool charges clinics 199 dollars a month.
We want a per seat price for bigger clinics next year.
I send Tidepool investors an update on the first Monday of each month.
The Tidepool hiring plan is one part time designer in January.
Tidepool can afford one hire before the seed round.
The Tidepool logo is a small wave in teal.
Tidepool plans to raise a seed round in the spring.
The seed round target is 1.5 million dollars.
Tidepool wants ten clinics by March.
Tidepool needs text reminders before the seed round.
Each pilot clinic got one Tidepool front desk tablet.
Tidepool had 400 weekly users in May and 800 in July.
Tidepool runs on Next.js and Postgres.
Tidepool has a waitlist of eleven clinics.
Clinics sign a three month pilot agreement with Tidepool.
The Tidepool team call is on Monday mornings.
Jordan Ellis charges a flat 600 dollars for the Tidepool logo.
Keep the Tidepool launch day talk under three minutes and end on the ask.
The Tidepool launch day talk is for Tidepool investors on December 2.
The launch talk opens with a clinic front desk story.
I applied to Stripe for the data analyst role.
The Stripe role is on the payments analytics team.
Stripe said I would hear back about the data analyst role in three weeks.
SkipDoodle is my weekend project, a drawing game for kids.
SkipDoodle is built with React Native and Expo, and Supabase stores the drawings.
SkipDoodle keeps each drawing as a small JSON file of strokes.
SkipDoodle keeps the drawing state in one hook, so undo stays simple.
SkipDoodle has three sticker packs: animals, space and food.
Kids unlock a sticker pack after ten drawings.
SkipDoodle uses eight bright colors and a rainbow brush.
SkipDoodle saves drawings offline and syncs them later.
SkipDoodle is waiting on App Store review.
The SkipDoodle listing has six screenshots.
Twelve families are testing SkipDoodle.
My cousin Ben tests SkipDoodle with his little sister.
SkipDoodle is free with one paid sticker pack.
SkipDoodle has no ads and no chat.
SkipDoodle can save a drawing to the photo album.
